prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1474; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just keep it to what happened, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. We'll keep your personal details off the recording. Can you tell me where the accident took place?

A: It was on a two-lane road in League City, Texas, near a shopping center. It was a slow weekday afternoon, and traffic was light.

Q: What were you doing right before the collision?

A: I was driving home from work. I was going maybe twenty-five miles an hour, because the road curves there and I always slow down.

Q: Tell me what happened next.

A: The other car came across into my lane. I think the driver was trying to pass something, but I'm not really sure. I hit the brakes and turned a little to the right, but we still made contact nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit. The airbags didn't go off.

Q: Did you feel any injury at the scene?

A: Not right away. I felt fine for maybe an hour. Then my neck started to stiffen up, and by that evening I had a dull headache and pain running into my shoulders.

Q: Have you sought medical care since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the next morning. They took X-rays, told me I had whiplash, and gave me a neck brace and some muscle relaxers. I've also been doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. Turning my head to the left is still hard, and I can't sit at a desk for long without it getting worse. Some mornings I wake up stiff.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I've been cooperative from the start and I'll send over the therapy bills and the urgent care paperwork whenever you need them.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
